# Celldega

> Linked, interactive visualization and analysis of spatial and single-cell omics.

Celldega pairs Python analysis with browser-based widgets for human-in-the-loop
work: you explore, select and annotate in the widgets, and the results come back
to Python for the next step. It sits downstream of Scanpy and Squidpy: most
functions take ``AnnData``, ``MuData`` or ``GeoDataFrame`` objects. It handles
Xenium (including Atera), MERSCOPE, Visium HD, CosMx and any single-cell
AnnData. Documentation: https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/ (an index for
AI agents is at https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/llms.txt).

Widgets (``celldega.viz``; the main ones are also on ``celldega``):

- ``Landscape``: the tissue (image, cells, transcripts, neighborhoods) or a UMAP.
- ``Clustergram``: an interactive clustered heatmap of a ``clust.Matrix``.
- ``Yearbook``: a grid of cell portraits for reviewing selected cells.
- ``Composition``: category counts or proportions compared across groups.
- ``CellCloud`` / ``NeighborhoodCloud``: 3D views of cells or neighborhood shapes.
- ``Enrich``: Enrichr gene-set enrichment of a gene list.
- ``Clerk``: an AI tool that interprets the linked widgets with Claude.

Link widgets with ``viz.spatial_clustergram``, ``viz.landscape_yearbook``,
``viz.landscape_yearbook_clustergram``, ``viz.clustergram_enrich`` or
``viz.link_clerk``. Save a view as a reproducible PNG with ``viz.snapshot`` and
rebuild it with ``viz.from_png``.

Analysis modules:

- ``pre``: instrument output to DegaFiles, which the browser streams a piece at a
  time (``pre.main``); 3D point-cloud and aligned H&E writers.
- ``clust``: ``Matrix``, hierarchical bi-clustering of any feature matrix for a
  Clustergram (``Matrix(adata, groupby="leiden")`` for cluster signatures).
- ``nbhd``: neighborhoods (alpha shapes, hextiles, gradients) and their
  composition, expression, overlap and bordering.
- ``set``, ``dataset``, ``collection``: collections of entities above the single
  cell (``SetCollection``, ``DatasetCollection``, ``NeighborhoodCollection``)
  and their feature spaces.
- ``select``: ``Selector`` queries and samples cells, for example for Yearbook.
- ``align``: stacks serial sections in 3D using the clusters they share.
- ``clerk``: the prompts and model calls behind the ``Clerk`` widget.

Example: a tissue linked to a heatmap of cluster signatures::

    import celldega as dega

    landscape = dega.Landscape(base_url=degafiles_url, adata=adata)
    mat = dega.clust.Matrix(adata, groupby="leiden")
    mat.cluster()
    cgm = dega.Clustergram(matrix=mat)
    dega.viz.spatial_clustergram(landscape, cgm)  # clicks in one update the other

## Docs

- [Home](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/): Celldega is a spatial and single-cell analysis and visualization library developed by the Spatial Technology Platform at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard.

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/): Celldega is a spatial and single-cell analysis and visualization library developed by the Spatial Technology Platform at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard.
- [Installation](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/installation/): Celldega supports Python 3.11 and 3.12. Install it into the environment used by your Jupyter notebook:
- [Visualize Your Own Data](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/your-data/): This guide follows a public 10x Genomics Xenium human pancreas dataset from the instrument's output to linked views of your own analysis: your clusters over the tissue and in a UMAP, a marker-gene dot plot, and gene-set…
- [From Scanpy & Squidpy](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/from-scanpy/): If you already analyze single-cell or spatial data with Scanpy and Squidpy, Celldega picks up where your notebook leaves off. It reads the same AnnData: your clusters, colors, UMAP, and expression.
- [Usage](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/usage/): Use Celldega in local or cloud notebooks, in a standalone web page, or through Celldega-App on your desktop.
- [Desktop App](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/desktop-app/): Celldega-App lets you explore prepared spatial and single-cell data on your desktop. Open a local or remote dataset, compare a Landscape with its linked Clustergram, or inspect cell portraits in a Yearbook.
- [Technologies](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/technologies/): Celldega utilizes a suite of complementary technologies to develop an efficient web-based analysis and visualization toolkit for spatial and single-cell data.
- [File Formats](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/getting-started/file_formats/): Celldega uses two complementary storage approaches: DegaFiles prepare spatial data for interactive rendering, and AnnData Zarr stores analysis inputs and visualization data.

## Visualizations

- [Visualizations](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/): Celldega's interactive views help you explore where cells are, how gene expression varies, and which biological processes distinguish a group.
- [Yearbook](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/yearbook/): `Yearbook` shows a grid of cell portraits: small, zoomed-in views of the tissue, each centered on one cell.
- [CellCloud](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/cell-cloud/): `CellCloud` shows cells in 3D, as points you can rotate and zoom.
- [NeighborhoodCloud](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/neighborhood-cloud/): `NeighborhoodCloud` is a 3D, orbit-camera view of precomputed tissue neighborhoods — one alpha-shape polygon per cluster/slice, so it stays cheap to display regardless of dataset size.
- [Clustergram](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/clustergram/): `Clustergram` uses hierarchical bi-clustering to organize both axes of a high-dimensional matrix: genes/features by their expression patterns, and cells, clusters, neighborhoods, or samples by their similarity.
- [Composition](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/composition/): `Composition` is a `Clustergram` variant for comparing category composition across groups — e.g. cell-type proportions across samples or conditions — rather than a general-purpose heatmap.
- [Enrich](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/enrich/): `Enrich` interprets a list of genes, such as the marker genes of a cluster, by looking them up in public gene-set libraries through Enrichr.
- [Landscape–Clustergram–Enrich](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/landscape-clustergram-enrich/): Link a Landscape, Clustergram, and Enrich to move between where cells are, which genes distinguish them, and what those genes mean.
- [CellCloud–Clustergram](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/cell-cloud-clustergram/): Link a CellCloud and Clustergram to compare 3D cell organization with gene-expression patterns.

## Visualizations: Landscape

- [Landscape](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/landscape/): `Landscape` shows where cells are and what they express.
- [UMAP and XY](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/landscape/umap-xy/): A Landscape can show cells in a low dimensional embedding, such as a UMAP, as well as in tissue. A UMAP places cells with similar expression near each other, so islands of cells suggest cell types and states.
- [Neighborhoods](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/landscape/neighborhoods/): Celldega helps you identify neighborhoods of cells, both in physical space, such as a structure in the tissue, and in data space, such as an island in a UMAP or a population in a two-gene XY plot.

## Visualizations: Clerk

- [Clerk](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/clerk/): The Clerk module (`celldega.clerk` and the `celldega.viz.Clerk` widget) is experimental. It is a proof of concept: its features, API and saved formats may change between releases, without deprecation.
- [Embedding Clerk](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/visualizations/clerk/hosting/): `celldega.clerk.run_turn` implements the bounded interpretation/evidence loop without widget traits, a browser transport or a model client. It consumes an initial model reply and yields plain-data events.

## Python API

- [Python API Overview](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/): Use Celldega to prepare visualization data, summarize analysis results, and explore them in linked widgets.
- [align](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/align/api/): Align serial tissue sections into a 3D stack of cells.
- [clerk](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/clerk/api/): Clerk -- Celldega's AI tool for exploring and interpreting its visualizations.
- [clust](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/clust/api/): Hierarchical bi-clustering of feature matrices, for Clustergrams.
- [collection](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/collection/api/): The base class of Celldega's collections of entities above the single cell, backed by MuData.
- [dataset](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/dataset/api/): Dataset-level collections: samples or datasets as observations, in several feature spaces.
- [nbhd](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/nbhd/api/): Neighborhoods: build tissue regions from cells, and summarize what is in them.
- [pre](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/pre/api/): Pre-process instrument output into DegaFiles, the files Celldega's browser widgets stream.
- [select](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/select/api/): Query and sample the cells (or other observations) of an AnnData, reproducibly.
- [set](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/set/api/): Set-level collections: sets of cells (clusters, domains, annotations) as observations.
- [viz](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/python/viz/api/): Interactive, linkable widgets for Jupyter, and helpers to link and save them.

## JavaScript API

- [JavaScript API Overview](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/javascript/): Use Celldega in a web page to explore prepared datasets without a Python kernel. The same Landscape and Clustergram views used in notebooks can read hosted DegaFiles or AnnData Zarr directly.
- [API](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/javascript/api/): The JavaScript component of Celldega is used within the Jupyter Widgets framework to provide interactive visualization in the context of a Jupyter notebook but can also be used as a standalone JavaScript library.
- [Viz API: getters, setters, exporters](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/javascript/viz-api/): Landscape and Clustergram expose an initial API for reading and changing views from code. Support varies by widget and control. Three kinds of methods cover this:
- [Portable Snapshots](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/javascript/saved-views/): Landscape and Clustergram expose `snapshot()` and `restore_snapshot()` independently of agent interfaces and notebook widgets. The goal is to preserve an interactive observation as reproducible visual evidence.

## JavaScript API: Development

- [State management](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/javascript/development/state-management/): How a Celldega visualization holds its state in the browser, how a change becomes a redraw, and what to follow when you add a control or embed Celldega in an application.

- [Tabula Sapiens UMAP and Cell-Type Signatures](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/gallery/gallery_tabula_sapiens_clustergram/): Explore the atlas alongside marker expression across 180 cell types. Click a Clustergram gene to color the UMAP, or a cell-type column to select its cells.

## Example Notebooks

- [Jupyter Notebook Examples](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/): These example notebooks demonstrate how to use Celldega to analyze and visualize spatial and single-cell data. Each notebook is designed to be run in a Jupyter environment and showcases different features of the library.

## Example Notebooks: Spatial Transcriptomics Tutorials

- [Atera Kidney Landscape-Clustergram](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Atera_Kidney_Landscape-Clustergram/): Compare the dataset's 28 default Leiden clusters in a linked Landscape–dotplot Clustergram, then measure how cell-type composition changes with distance from podocyte-defined glomerular footprints.
- [Atera Brain Hippocampus H&E Landscape-Matrix](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Atera_Brain_Hippocampus_Landscape-Matrix/): Explore the pre-processed 10x Genomics Atera WTA dataset `Atera_v1_WTA_S4A_Brain_Hippocampus_ND_FF` with Celldega:
- [Atera Breast Cancer FF H&E Landscape-Matrix](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Atera_Breast_Cancer_Landscape-Matrix/): Explore the pre-processed 10x Genomics Atera WTA dataset `Atera_v1_WTA_S4C_Breast_Cancer_FF` with Celldega:
- [Atera Colorectal Cancer H&E Landscape-Matrix](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Atera_Colorectal_Cancer_Landscape-Matrix/): Explore the pre-processed 10x Genomics Atera WTA dataset `Atera_v1_WTA_S4B_Colorectal_Cancer_FF` with Celldega:
- [Atera Breast Cancer Landscape-Clustergram](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Atera_Breast_Cancer_Landscape-Clustergram/): This tutorial uses `celldega>=0.26.0`.
- [Atera Breast Cancer Neighborhood Exploration](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Atera_Breast_Cancer_Neighborhood_Exploration/): Continue from the Atera Landscape–Clustergram tutorial. Run its data preprocessing first; this notebook reuses the saved cell list, 10x cell types and tissue coordinates. Requires `celldega>=0.26.0`.
- [Visium HD Human CRC Landscape-Clustergram-Enrich](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Visium_HD_Human_CRC_Landscape-Clustergram-Enrich/): This tutorial explores a Visium HD human colorectal cancer (CRC) sample that was already segmented into cells and clustered with Scanpy (220,703 cells, 15 Leiden clusters). It shows the handoff from Scanpy to Celldega:
- [Scanpy-Squidpy Xenium Pancreas](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Scanpy-Squidpy_Xenium_Pancreas/): https://squidpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/notebooks/tutorials/tutorial_xenium.html#analyze-xenium-data

## Example Notebooks: Spatial Transcriptomics Tutorials: 3D Spatial Transcriptomics

- [Broad-Allen Mouse Brain Preprocessing and Alignment](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Broad-Allen_Dev-Mouse-Brain_E15.5_Align/): This tutorial uses Celldega 0.29 (`pip install "celldega>=0.29"`). It shows how Celldega aligns serial sections into a 3D stack in two simple steps, using the Leiden clusters as landmarks:
- [Broad-Allen Mouse Brain Visualization](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Broad-Allen_Dev-Mouse-Brain_E15.5_Viz/): This tutorial uses Celldega `0.28.0a5` and the matching JavaScript package `0.28.0-alpha.5`. It visualizes a 3D alignment of the serial sections.

## Example Notebooks: Single Cell Tutorials

- [Chromium PBMC Landscape-Clustergram-Enrich](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Scanpy_Chromium/): Cluster the 10x Genomics Chromium PBMC 3k dataset with Scanpy, save the AnnData to Zarr, and explore it with Celldega:
- [Tabula Sapiens Atlas Landscape-Clustergram-Enrich](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/tutorial_notebooks/Tabula_Sapiens_Landscape-Clustergram-Enrich/): CELLxGENE Discover's homepage sends you to Tabula Sapiens - All Cells in its Explorer: 1,136,218 cells from 28 organs of 24 donors, on the authors' UMAP.

## Example Notebooks: Brief Notebooks

- [Landscape View Xenium](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Landscape_View_Xenium/)
- [Landscape from a Local Server](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Landscape_Local_Server/): Celldega's widgets run in the browser and load DegaFiles (the output of `dega.pre.main`) over HTTP.
- [Atera Pre-process](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Atera_Pre-process/): Make DegaFiles from a 10x Atera output bundle.
- [Atera Pre-process with H&E](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Atera_Pre-process_with_HE/): Turn a 10x Genomics Atera WTA output bundle into Celldega DegaFiles, and add the post-run H&E image as an aligned background.
- [Atera Kidney Yearbook Review](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Atera_Kidney_Yearbook_Review/): Use a tissue-wide Landscape for context, then send candidate cell IDs to a paginated Yearbook. Select the portraits that deserve a closer look and get their IDs back in Python.
- [Atera Kidney Low-Quality Cell Review](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Atera_Kidney_Low_Quality_Review/): Removing cells with few transcripts and a small area is a standard quality control step, but its thresholds are usually chosen from histograms alone.
- [Atera Kidney Ectopic Expression Review](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Atera_Kidney_Ectopic_Expression_Review/): Ectopic expression is a cell expressing marker genes of a different cell type.
- [Atera Kidney Clerk Case](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Atera_Kidney_Clerk_Case/): Clerk is Celldega's AI tool for interpreting its visualizations.
- [CellCloud Thick MERFISH](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Landscape-3D_thick_MERFISH/): Data obtained from https://elifesciences.org/reviewed-preprints/90029v1
- [Landscape-Heatmap Visium-HD](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Landscape-Heatmap-Visium-HD/)
- [UMAP-Cluster Pancreas Xenium](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/UMAP-Cluster_Pancreas_Xenium/): https://squidpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/notebooks/tutorials/tutorial_xenium.html#analyze-xenium-data
- [Custom Segmentation](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Custom_Segmentation/): Data source: https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/xenium-prime-ffpe-human-skin
- [Gradient Neighborhood Pancreas Islets](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/Gradient_Neighborhood_Pancreas_Islets/): This notebook demonstrates the gradient neighborhood workflow in `celldega.nbhd`.
- [DatasetCollection Feature Spaces](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/DatasetCollection_Feature_Spaces/): A `DatasetCollection` makes samples the observations and stores each feature space calculated for them as a modality (see Collections).
- [SetCollection Compare Clusterings](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/SetCollection_Compare_Clusterings/): A `SetCollection` makes sets of cells, such as clusters, the observations, and keeps exactly which cells are in each set.
- [SetCollection Signatures Dot Plot](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/SetCollection_Signatures/): A `SetCollection` derives feature spaces from the cells in each set. `calc_signature` calculates each set's mean expression and, optionally, the fraction of its cells that express each gene, in one modality.
- [NeighborhoodCollection Hexagonal Niches](https://broadinstitute.github.io/celldega/examples/brief_notebooks/NeighborhoodCollection_Hextile_Niches/): A `NeighborhoodCollection` holds neighborhoods with their geometry and the feature spaces calculated for them.
